fullPassage: According to Aristotle, the world has two distinct regions, the terrestrial and the celestial. Each region is characterized by specific material elements and motions. There are four elements in the terrestrial region - Earth, Water, Air, and Fire - differentiated by the primary contrary qualities of hot, cold, dry, and moist. Natural motions in the terrestrial region are rectilinear, and these four elements either move away from or towards the center of the cosmos: Fire and Air move away from the center while Earth and Water move towards it. The physical bodies encountered in everyday life are not the elements, but are each a sort of compound, containing at least two of the elements; it may even be the case that all compound bodies contain all four elements. What we know as everyday, ordinary 'earth' is a compound composed of the elements Earth, Water, Fire, and Air. There is a fifth element that is the stuff of the celestial bodies whose natural motion is circular; that element, in the celestial region, is known as aither (or aether, in Latin). The aither varies in purity, being more pure where it is more distant from the terrestrial elements and less pure in closer proximity to them. The four terrestrial elements are themselves material causes, while the motion of the continually moving bodies in the celestial sphere is the efficient cause of some terrestrial events. In other words, there is interaction between the regions, and the celestial region can affect the terrestrial. The motion of the aither causes material in the terrestrial realm to be heated. For example, rain is due to the efficient cause of the Sun's motion as it gets closer to or more distant from the Earth, and the subsequent processes of evaporation and condensation.

There are four elements in the terrestrial region - Earth, Water, Air, and Fire - differentiated by the primary contrary qualities of hot, cold, dry, and moist. Natural motions in the terrestrial region are rectilinear, and these four elements either move away from or towards the center of the cosmos: Fire and Air move away from the center while Earth and Water move towards it. The physical bodies encountered in everyday life are not the elements, but are each a sort of <u>compound</u>, containing at least two of the elements; it may even be the case that all compound bodies contain all four elements. What we know as everyday, ordinary 'earth' is a compound composed of the elements Earth, Water, Fire, and Air. There is a fifth element that is the stuff of the celestial bodies whose natural motion is circular; that element, in the celestial region, is known as aither (or aether, in Latin). The aither varies in purity, being more pure where it is more distant from the terrestrial elements and less pure in closer proximity to them. The four terrestrial elements are themselves material causes, while the motion of the continually moving bodies in the celestial sphere is the efficient cause of some terrestrial events. In other words, there is interaction between the regions, and the celestial region can affect the terrestrial. The motion of the aither causes material in the terrestrial realm to be heated. For example, rain is due to the efficient cause of the Sun's motion as it gets closer to or more distant from the Earth, and the subsequent processes of evaporation and condensation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 compound와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: compound = (여러 원소가 섞인) 화합물, 혼합물 → mixture
det.analysis:
✅ ① mixture — 혼합물, 화합물 ←정답 (적어도 두 원소를 포함하는 것)
❌ ② element — 원소 (본문에서 compound와 대비되는 반대 개념)
❌ ③ motion — 운동 (의미축 다름)
❌ ④ surface — 표면 (의미축 다름)
det.tip: compound ≈ mixture(둘 이상의 원소가 결합된 것)

questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 body의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) the patient's body = 몸, 신체 / (B) each body in the night sky = (하늘의) 천체, 물체
det.analysis:
✅ ① 몸, 신체 — (하늘의) 천체, 물체 ←정답
❌ ② (하늘의) 천체 — 몸, 신체 (A와 B가 뒤바뀜)
❌ ③ 몸, 신체 — 단체, 조직 (B는 '조직'이 아니라 '천체')
❌ ④ 시신, 사체 — 본문, 내용 (둘 다 문맥과 무관)
det.tip: body: (A) 신체 vs (B) 천체(하늘의 물체) — 본문의 celestial bodies와 같은 뜻

questions.passage: There are four elements in the terrestrial region - Earth, Water, Air, and Fire - __________ (differentiate) by the primary contrary qualities of hot, cold, dry, and moist. Natural motions in the terrestrial region are rectilinear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 네 원소가 성질에 의해 '구별되는' 것이므로, 원소를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사 differentiated로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: four elements ... __________ (differentiate) by ... → 원소가 성질에 의해 '구별되는' 대상이므로 과거분사 differentiated (수동 의미의 분사 후치수식)

questions.passage: The physical bodies encountered in everyday life are not the elements, but are each a sort of compound, containing at least two of the elements. What we know as everyday, ordinary 'earth' is a compound __________ (compose) of the elements Earth, Water, Fire, and Air.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: '흙'이 네 원소로 '구성된' 화합물이라는 뜻이므로, compound를 수식하는 과거분사 composed로 바꾼다. be composed of = ~로 구성되다.
det.analysis: a compound __________ (compose) of the elements → '~로 구성된'을 뜻하는 과거분사 composed. be/compound composed of = ~로 이루어진

det.korean: 지상의 네 원소는 그 자체로 '질료인(material causes)'인 반면, 천구의 운동은 작용인(efficient cause)이라는 대비 구조이다.
det.analysis:

❌ ④ celestial bodies — 천체 (지상 원소와 반대 영역)
det.tip: 지상 원소 = material causes(질료인) ↔ 천구 운동 = efficient cause(작용인)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 네 원소는 뜨거움·차가움·건조함·습함이라는 '기본적인 상반된 성질(the primary contrary qualities)'에 의해 구별된다. 빈칸 뒤에 그 성질 목록이 나온다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② the primary contrary qualities — 기본적인 상반된 성질 ←정답 (바로 뒤 hot, cold, dry, moist가 그 성질)
❌ ① the four natural motions — 네 가지 자연 운동 (뒤의 성질 목록과 안 맞음)
❌ ③ the celestial bodies' paths — 천체의 궤도 (지상 원소 구별과 무관)
❌ ④ the subsequent processes — 뒤따르는 과정 (비 형성 관련, 원소 구별과 무관)
det.tip: differentiated by ___ of hot, cold, dry, and moist → 그 짝은 상반된 성질(qualities)
